name: Joan of Arc
label: Jade Tree
lede: Twenty-five years, one permanent member and a revolving cast of dozens: Tim Kinsella's band broke up after its first show, got a 1.9 from Pitchfork, picked collaborators out of a hat and rewrote Orwell with its own names in it.

eras.title: Broke up after the first show
eras.text: When Cap'n Jazz fell apart, Tim Kinsella started again right away and nearly ended it just as fast. The band that became Joan of Arc threw out everything after one gig, then made a debut that listeners either loved or found hideous.

years.h: Red Blue Yellow plays one show, quits, and becomes Joan of Arc
years.p: Tim Kinsella's post-Cap'n Jazz band starts as Red Blue Yellow, breaks up after its first show, throws out all its songs and starts over. Three months later Joan of Arc debuts at Chicago's Autonomous Zone.

years.h: Two 7-inches, then a Jade Tree deal
years.p: Two early Joan of Arc singles get the band signed to Jade Tree, the Delaware label already home to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]].

years.h: A Portable Model Of: acoustic songs, strange electronics
years.p: Joan of Arc's debut was recorded in Chicago at Elliot's Loft and Idful Music, with [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]] and Ryan Rapsys of Euphone among the guests. AllMusic said most listeners would love it or find it hideous.
play: I Love a Woman (Who Loves Me)

eras.title: Pro Tools, a 1.9 and a breakup
eras.text: Joan of Arc went further into the machine: laptops, samples, songs built from over 100 tracks. The critics split hard, Jade Tree lost confidence, and in 2001 Kinsella shut it down and went back to his Cap'n Jazz bandmates.

years.h: How Memory Works: Jeremy Boyle's laptop joins the band
years.p: Synthetic noise and vocal samples cut between songs. [[Jeremy Boyle|3b67e0f4-9eed-4e5e-bf93-2638afa046c2]] brought laptop and software work from his art training at the University of Illinois at Chicago.

years.h: Live in Chicago, 1999 isn't a live album
years.p: Joan of Arc's title only meant that the band lived in Chicago in 1999. Joan of Arc liked to make titles and artwork misleading, funny or confusing on purpose.

years.h: The Gap: all Pro Tools, 1.9 from Pitchfork
years.p: Made entirely in Pro Tools between October 1999 and June 2000, with some songs over 100 tracks. Pitchfork gave it 1.9, Spin an 8.
years.xp:
The cover nods to Jean-Luc Godard's 1967 film Weekend. The Chicago Tribune called The Gap frustrating, daring and sometimes unlistenable, and PopMatters wondered whether it was one of the most unlistenable albums ever made.

Tim Kinsella didn't help himself. In promotional interviews he insisted on asking the questions, which may have added to the bad reviews.

years.big: Tensions, a flop EP, and the label gives up
years.h: Joan of Arc breaks up as Jade Tree loses confidence
years.p: Growing tension in the band, Jade Tree's loss of confidence and a poorly received EP after The Gap end Joan of Arc for the first time.

years.h: Tim Kinsella's Owls: a Cap'n Jazz reunion in all but name
years.p: Tim and [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]], Sam Zurick and [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] release [[Owls|f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2]] on Jade Tree, recorded with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The band splits after one tour.

eras.title: Back from the dead, names out of a hat
eras.text: Joan of Arc came back with guitars and grew into a collective: Califone members, cousins, anyone who had ever been in the band. Kinsella moved to Polyvinyl, made a feature film, and kept a second band, Make Believe, going at the same time.

years.h: So Much Staying Alive and Lovelessness: back, with guitars
years.p: Made with Sam Zurick and Mike Kinsella, Joan of Arc's return is a guitar record, nothing like The Gap. AllMusic called it a return to form. It's the band's last album for Jade Tree.

years.h: In Rape Fantasy and Terror Sex We Trust, produced by Califone
years.p: From the same sessions, a darker, collaged Joan of Arc record on Perishable, made with [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]]'s [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]] and Ben Massarella.

years.h: Bobby Burg and Nate Kinsella join; Make Believe starts
years.p: For touring, Tim Kinsella adds bassist [[Bobby Burg|928e4971-5c1a-421a-8ef5-7c1fc74c03b0]] and his cousin [[Nate Kinsella|dee29ad9-ba52-4af1-8372-4acbfb725554]] alongside Sam Zurick. The same four also run [[Make Believe|82d7935d-c121-43e3-8f33-ed999f9357f8]] until 2008.

years.h: Joan of Arc, Dick Cheney, Mark Twain · Polyvinyl
years.p: Joan of Arc's first Polyvinyl album brings in a huge team of collaborators and draws some of the band's best reviews.

years.cap: Joan of Arc Presents Guitar Duets
years.h: Guitar Duets: ten ex-members, partners picked from a hat
years.p: Tim Kinsella gathers ten former Joan of Arc members and friends, including [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]], pulls names from a hat to make pairs, and has each pair record a guitar duet. Tracks are identified only by the pair's faces.

years.h: Tim Kinsella's film Orchard Vale opens in Chicago
years.p: Kinsella's feature Orchard Vale, released as Joan of Arc Presents Orchard Vale, premieres at the Chicago Underground Film Festival.

years.h: Boo! Human: 14 musicians, one of the band's most cohesive
years.p: Joan of Arc uses 14 players on its Polyvinyl album. Drummer [[Theo Katsaounis|31133026-476a-42f5-9d17-5d20f62e93fe]] joins in 2008 and stays to the end.

eras.title: Joyful Noise and the last lineup
eras.text: On Joyful Noise, Joan of Arc settled into a steady four-piece and got more conceptual than ever: Bowie sampled into collage, a vocalist who took over the mic, a novel rewritten with the band as characters. In 2020 Kinsella ended it after 25 years.

years.h: Every Joan of Arc album on cassette, in one box
years.p: Joyful Noise Recordings issues a ten-album cassette box set running from A Portable Model Of (1997) through Flowers (2009).

years.h: Life Like: back to basics as a four-piece
years.p: A four-piece Joan of Arc and more regular touring than any recent line-up. The same year, Oh Brother collects four unfinished albums, with [[Zach Hill|df6a1106-6caf-465b-bcfd-0b80d2b53516]] among the players.

years.h: Tim Kinsella's first novel, published by Featherproof
years.p: Featherproof Books publishes The Karaoke Singer's Guide to Self-Defense. A second novel, Let Go and Go On and On, follows in 2014.

years.h: Melina Ausikaitis joins Joan of Arc
years.p: Vocalist and guitarist [[Melina Ausikaitis|fb3dcb42-f50c-4a80-a4f8-098c42be0caa]] joins Tim Kinsella, Bobby Burg and Theo Katsaounis, completing the last line-up.

years.h: Hunky Dory TK, built entirely from David Bowie samples
years.p: During Tim Kinsella's residency at Joyful Noise, Joan of Arc makes an electronic collage entirely from [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]]'s Hunky Dory. It's performed at Chicago's Museum of Contemporary Art during the David Bowie Is exhibition.

years.h: He's Got the Whole This Land Is Your Land in His Hands
years.p: Some critics dismissed the Joyful Noise album. Others rank it among Joan of Arc's most ambitious and fully realized experiments.

years.h: 1984: Melina Ausikaitis sings, and Orwell gets rewritten
years.p: Ausikaitis takes lead vocals on some songs. Joyful Noise printed a version of Nineteen Eighty-Four set in Chicago, with Winston Smith renamed Tim Kinsella and O'Brien renamed Bobby Burg.
years.xp: Kinsella said the record alternates the way a late Black Flag album does: Ausikaitis sings a song, then the band jams. The rewritten novel was posted on 1984.com for a limited time.

years.h: Joan of Arc announces its final album, Tim Melina Theo Bobby
years.p: Named for the last four members, Tim Melina Theo Bobby comes out December 4, 2020, and ends Joan of Arc after 25 years.
